title: Introducing yourself (Sich vorstellen)
summary: Say who you are and ask others: name, country, city, languages, job.
goals: Say your name, where you come from and where you live
Ask someone the same questions, politely (Sie) or to a friend (du)
Use heißen, kommen and wohnen in the present tense

videos.title: What a verb is: stem and ending

sections.title: Three verbs to start with
sections.text:
To introduce yourself you need three verbs: [[heißen]] (to be called), [[kommen]] (to come) and [[wohnen]] (to live).

One rule builds the present tense of almost every verb: drop **-en** from the infinitive to get the stem ([[wohnen]] minus -en = wohn-), then add the ending for the person: **ich -e, du -st, er/sie/es -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie/Sie -en**. So [[ich wohne]], [[du wohnst]], [[er wohnt]]. The wir and sie/Sie forms look just like the infinitive. The few exceptions, like [[sein]] (lesson 3), get their own tables.

Three questions and their answers:
- [[Wie heißen Sie?]] - [[Ich heiße Hayk.]]
- [[Woher kommen Sie?]] - [[Ich komme aus Armenien.]]
- [[Wo wohnen Sie?]] - [[Ich wohne in München.]]

In every sentence the verb is the *second* part.

One trap: the stem of [[heißen]] already ends in ß, so the du form adds only **-t**: [[du heißt]], not 'heißst'.

items.de: Mein Vorname ist Hayk. Mein Nachname ist Tarkhanyan.
items.en: My first name is Hayk. My surname is Tarkhanyan.

items.de: Ich spreche Armenisch, Russisch und Englisch.
items.en: I speak Armenian, Russian and English.
What do you do for a living?

sections.title: heißen, kommen, wohnen in the present tense

sections.text:
Like Russian and Armenian, German changes the verb for each person: [[ich wohne]], [[du wohnst]] - я живу, ты живёшь - ես ապրում եմ, դու ապրում ես.

German also has two ways to say *you*, like Russian **ты / Вы** and Armenian **դու / Դուք**: [[du]] for friends, [[Sie]] (always with a capital S) for colleagues you don't know well.

Answer with the same verb as the question, then ask back: [[Woher kommen Sie?]] - [[Ich komme aus Armenien. Und Sie?]] With a friend: [[Und du?]] ([[Und dir?]] and [[Und Ihnen?]] from Unit 0 are only for [[Wie geht's?]].)
Write every noun with a capital letter: [[der Name]], [[das Land]], [[die Sprache]]. Country names too: [[Armenien]], [[Deutschland]].

items.en: What do you do for a living?

items.question: How do you ask a colleague's name politely?
items.explanation: Sie is the polite form; du is for friends.

items.instruction: Fill in the gaps: I come from Armenia and I live in Munich.
items.text: Ich ___ aus Armenien und ich ___ in München.
items.explanation: With ich the verb ends in -e: ich komme, ich wohne.

items.instruction: A new verb, same rule. Fill in the gap with lernen: He is learning German.
items.explanation: lernen minus -en = lern-, and er takes -t: er lernt. The same as er wohnt.
Question word first, then the verb, then Sie.
